# central.dogma Package

Tools for working with the central dogma of molecular biology, from DNA to RNA to protein. The package provides functions for splitting a DNA sequence into codons in a chosen reading frame, which is the first step in translating a coding sequence into its amino acid sequence. It also provides a plot of Amino Acid frequency, which makes it easy to view the composition of the sequnence.

# Function 1- sampling function

This generates a random DNA sequence. Takes a specified length and builds a synthetic DNA template strand by randomly sampling nucleotide bases (`A`, `T`, `G`, `C`) with replacement. The `seq_length` argument determines the total number of bases in the output. The result is a single character string representing a foundational genetic sequence, ready for use as the upstream template in downstream transcription and translation.

# Function 2 - substituteT4U function

Converts a DNA sequence into an RNA sequence

The substituteT4U function takes a DNA sequence represented as a character string and replaces every occurrence of the nucleotide thymine (T) with uracil (U), producing an RNA sequence. This shows the difference between DNA and RNA, because RNA contains uracil instead of thymine. The function preserves the sequence length and the order of all nucleotides, leaving the other characters unchanged. The resulting RNA sequence can then be passed to the getCodon function to split it into codons for translation into amino acids.

# Function 3 - getCodon Function

Split a DNA sequence into codons

Takes a single DNA sequence and cuts it into consecutive, non-overlapping three-letter codons. The \`start\` argument sets the reading frame (1, 2 or 3), so reading can begin at any of the first three bases. Any leftover bases at the end that cannot form a full codon are dropped. The result is a character vector with one codon per element, ready for use in translation to amino acids

# Function 4- translateRNA Function

Translate a sequence of codons into an amino acid string

Takes a character vector containing consecutive three-letter RNA codons and translates them into their corresponding amino acids. The function maps the provided sequence against the standard genetic code table stored internally within the package. The individual amino acid characters are then collapsed and pasted together without any separators. The result is a single character string representing the fully translated protein sequence, completing the simulated central dogma pipeline.

# Function 5 - Amino Acid Frequency Plot

Creates a bar plot showing the frequency of amino acids in a protein sequence. Takes a single protein sequence as input, identifies each unique amino acid present, and counts how many times it occurs within the sequence. These counts are organised into a data frame and visualised as a ggplot2 bar chart, where each bar represents the frequency of a particular amino acid. The function returns the completed ggplot object, allowing it to be displayed or further customised by the user.
